rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet prayed seated in voluntary prayer during the year before his death, according to Muslim’s report.
rows.anchor: كان صلى الله عليه وسلم يصلي قاعدا قبل موته بعام في النافلة

rows.speaker: عائشة
rows.claim: Aisha reported seeing the Prophet pray cross-legged; al-Nasa’i transmitted her report.
rows.anchor: عن عائشة رضي الله عنها قالت: رأيت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يصلي متربعا

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الرحمن
rows.claim: Abu Abd al-Rahman says only Abu Dawud al-Hafri, whom he considers trustworthy, transmitted the report, and he suspects it is mistaken.
rows.anchor: قال أبو عبد الرحمن: لا أعلم أحدا روى هذا الحديث غير أبي داود الحفري وهو ثقة،

rows.speaker: مالك
rows.claim: Malik’s reported ruling is that a seated worshipper sits cross-legged for the standing portion and adopts prostration as far as able when prostrating.
rows.anchor: عن مالك أنه يتربع في قيامه، وقاله البويطي عن الشافعي

rows.speaker: الثوري والليث وأحمد وإسحاق وأبو يوسف ومحمد
rows.claim: Sufyan, al-Layth, Ahmad, Ishaq, Abu Yusuf, and Muhammad share the posture ruling allowing the seated worshipper to prostrate as able, including in voluntary prayer.
rows.anchor: ونحوه قول الثوري، وكذلك قال الليث وأحمد وإسحاق وأبو يوسف ومحمد

rows.speaker: الشافعي
rows.claim: In the narration transmitted by al-Muzani, al-Shafi‘i says the seated worshipper remains seated like the tashahhud throughout prayer.
rows.anchor: وقال الشافعي في رواية المزني: يجلس في صلاته كلها كجلوس التشهد

rows.speaker: أبو سلمة بن عبد الرحمن
rows.claim: Abu Salama interprets this verse’s ribat as waiting for one prayer after another, noting there were no military frontiers to guard in the Prophet’s time.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو سلمة بن عبد الرحمن هذه الآية في انتظار الصلاة بعد الصلاة،

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet describes ablution through hardship, walking to mosques, and waiting for the next prayer as acts that erase sins and raise ranks, calling them ribat three times.
rows.anchor: وكثرة الخطا إلى المساجد وانتظار الصلاة بعد الصلاة فذلكم الرباط

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn Atiyya holds that ribat properly means remaining in God’s path at a frontier; the prayer hadith compares waiting to military ribat.
rows.anchor: والقول الصحيح هو أن الرباط هو الملازمة في سبيل الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qurtubi rejects Ibn Atiyya’s restriction of the lexical meaning: al-Khalil says ribat also means keeping to prayer, so waiting for prayer is literally ribat.
rows.anchor: فإن الخليل بن أحمد أحد أئمة اللغة وثقاتها قد قال: الرباط ملازمة الثغور،

rows.speaker: الشيباني
rows.claim: Al-Shaybani’s description of enduring water as murabit, reported by Ibn Faris, supports a broad lexical sense of something held in place.
rows.anchor: أنه يقال: ماء مترابط أي دائم لا ينزح حكاه ابن فارس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ribat is binding something so it does not loosen; it disciplines the heart in good intention and the body in obedience, especially through horses at the frontier and constancy in prayer.
rows.anchor: فإن المرابطة عند العرب: العقد على الشيء حتى لا ينحل،

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة وجابر وعلي
rows.claim: Reports from Abu Hurayra, Jabir, and Ali apply the Prophet’s term ribat to keeping oneself attached to the prayers.
rows.anchor: وارتباط النفس على الصلوات كما قاله النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم رواه أبو هريرة وجابر وعلي

rows.speaker: محمد بن المواز
rows.claim: For jurists, a murabit is one who travels to a frontier and stays there for a period to guard it.
rows.anchor: هو الذي يشخص إلى ثغر من الثغور ليرابط فيه مدة ما قاله محمد بن المواز

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn Atiyya distinguishes permanent frontier residents who live and earn there with families: they protect the border but are not technically murabitun.
rows.anchor: فهم وإن كانوا حماة فليسوا بمرابطين. قاله ابن عطية

rows.speaker: ابن خويز منداد
rows.claim: Ibn Khuzaymandad permits families at a secure, fortified frontier; at an unsafe frontier a qualified fighter may guard personally but should not bring family liable to capture.
rows.anchor: حالة يكون الثغر مأمونا منيعا يجوز سكناه بالأهل والولد. وإن كان غير مأمون جاز أن يرابط فيه بنفسه

rows.speaker: سهل بن سعد الساعدي
rows.claim: Al-Bukhari transmits from Sahl ibn Sa‘d that the Prophet said one day of guarding the frontier is better than the world and all it contains.
rows.anchor: منها ما رواه البخاري عن سهل بن سعد الساعدي أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet says one day guarding the frontier in God’s path is better with God than the world and everything in it.
rows.anchor: رباط يوم في سبيل الله خير عند الله من الدنيا وما فيها

rows.speaker: سلمان
rows.claim: The Prophet says a day and night of ribat surpass a month of fasting and prayer; the reward continues after death, with provision and protection from grave trials.
rows.anchor: وفي صحيح مسلم عن سلمان قال سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول:

rows.speaker: فضالة بن عبيد
rows.claim: The Prophet says a murabit’s deeds continue to grow until Resurrection and he is protected from the grave’s interrogator, unlike other dead people.
rows.anchor: وروى أبو داود في سننه عن فضالة بن عبيد أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: These reports show ribat among the best deeds whose reward continues after death, unlike the three ongoing deeds whose effects end when their causes cease.
rows.anchor: وفي هذين الحديثين دليل على أن الرباط أفضل الأعمال التي يبقى ثوابها بعد الموت

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: The Prophet names ongoing charity, useful knowledge, and a righteous child’s prayer as the three deeds continuing after a person dies; Muslim alone transmits this sound report.
rows.anchor: كما جاء في حديث العلاء بن عبد الرحمن عن أبيه عن أبي هريرة عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ribat’s reward multiplies until Resurrection without depending on a cause that later expires, because guarding the faith enables all other acts of worship and Islamic rites.
rows.anchor: والرباط يضاعف أجره إلى يوم القيامة لأنه لا معنى للنماء إلا المضاعفة

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: A sound Ibn Majah report says dying while guarding the frontier earns the person the continuing reward of his usual good works and protection through Resurrection.
rows.anchor: من مات مرابطا في سبيل الله أجرى عليه أجر عمله الصالح الذي كان يعمل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qurtubi notes that the continuing reward in this report is specifically conditioned on dying while engaged in ribat.
rows.anchor: وفي هذا الحديث قيد ثان وهو الموت حالة الرباط

rows.speaker: عثمان بن عفان
rows.claim: A report from Uthman attributes to the Prophet that one night of ribat equals a thousand nights of fasting and prayer.
rows.anchor: وروي عن عثمان بن عفان قال: سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some read the first repentance verse as applying to every sinner; others limit it to sin committed in ignorance, while repentance for all sins is stated elsewhere.
rows.anchor: قيل: هذه الآية عامة لكل من عمل ذنبا. وقيل: لمن جهل فقط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The whole community agrees that believers must repent, as commanded in the verse about all believers returning to God.
rows.anchor: واتفقت الأمة على أن التوبة فرض على المؤمنين

rows.speaker: أهل السنة
rows.claim: A person can repent of one sin while continuing another of a different kind; Sunnis see no distinction among sins on this point.
rows.anchor: وتصح من ذنب مع الإقامة على غيره من غير نوعه خلافا للمعتزلة

rows.speaker: المعتزلة
rows.claim: The Mu‘tazilites deny that a person has repented from one sin while persisting in another.
rows.anchor: خلافا للمعتزلة في قولهم: لا يكون تائبا من أقام على ذنب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reason does not obligate God to accept repentance, because no one can stand at a higher rank than the Creator who owns and charges creation.
rows.anchor: وليس قبول التوبة واجبا على الله من طريق العقل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s truthful scriptural promise establishes acceptance of repentance as a promised obligation, while the doctrine denies any obligation upon Him by reason.
rows.anchor: فإخباره سبحانه وتعالى عن أشياء أوجبها على نفسه يقتضي وجوب تلك الأشياء

rows.speaker: أبو المعالي
rows.claim: Abu al-Ma‘ali and others say the scriptural promises yield strong expectation, not certainty, that God will accept repentance.
rows.anchor: قال أبو المعالي وغيره: وهذه الظواهر إنما تعطي غلبة ظن، لا قطعا على الله تعالى بقبول التوبة

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn Atiyya prefers certainty that God accepts a fully sincere repentance, following his father and God’s explicit promises and mercy.
rows.anchor: وكان أبي رحمه الله يميل إلى هذا القول ويرجحه وبه أقول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase ‘upon God’ is elliptical for God’s grace and mercy toward His servants, not a literal duty imposed on Him.
rows.anchor: وإنما المعنى على فضل الله ورحمته بعباده. وهذا نحو

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet’s exchange with Mu‘adh about the servants’ right upon God means a promise grounded in God’s grace and mercy.
rows.anchor: قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم لمعاذ: «أتدري ما حق العباد على الله»

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘Upon’ may mean ‘with’; either way God promises without failing that He accepts repentance meeting its valid conditions.
rows.anchor: وقيل: «على» ها هنا معناها «عند» والمعنى واحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Valid repentance requires heartfelt regret, stopping the sin immediately, resolving not to repeat it, and acting from shame before God alone; missing any condition invalidates it.
rows.anchor: وهي أربعة الندم بالقلب، وترك المعصية في الحال، والعزم على ألا يعود إلى مثلها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some add confession of the sin and frequent seeking of forgiveness as repentance conditions.
rows.anchor: وقد قيل من شروطها: الاعتراف بالذنب وكثرة الاستغفار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Repentance does not cancel a fixed legal penalty: if testimony establishes theft or slander, the prescribed penalty is carried out despite repentance.
rows.anchor: ولا خلاف فيما أعلمه أن التوبة لا تسقط حدا ولهذا قال علماؤنا: إن السارق والسارقة والقاذف متى تابوا

rows.speaker: أبو بكر بن عبدوس
rows.claim: Abu Bakr ibn Abdus offers another reading: ‘upon’ means ‘from,’ so repentance comes from God.
rows.anchor: وقيل: «على» بمعنى «من» أي إنما التوبة من الله للذين قاله أبو بكر بن عبدوس،

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada says the Prophet’s Companions agreed that every disobedience is committed in ignorance, whether deliberate or uninformed.
rows.anchor: قال قتادة: أجمع أصحاب النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم على أن كل معصية فهي بجهالة، عمدا كانت أو جهلا

rows.speaker: ابن عباس وقتادة والضحاك ومجاهد والسدي
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas, Qatada, al-Dahhak, Mujahid, and al-Suddi hold that ‘in ignorance’ covers every sin, since every sinner is ignorant until leaving the sin.
rows.anchor: فكل من عصى ربه فهو جاهل حتى ينزع عن معصيته

rows.speaker: الضحاك ومجاهد
rows.claim: A report from al-Dahhak and Mujahid interprets ‘in ignorance’ specifically as deliberate action.
rows.anchor: وروي عن الضحاك ومجاهد أنهما قالا: الجهالة هنا العمد.

rows.speaker: عكرمة
rows.claim: Ikrima calls worldly preoccupations outside obedience ignorance, aligning this view with the verse describing worldly life as play and diversion.
rows.anchor: أمور الدنيا كلها جهالة يريد الخاصة بها الخارجة عن طاعة الله

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj explains ignorance as choosing fleeting pleasure over lasting pleasure.
rows.anchor: وقال الزجاج: يعني قوله «بجهالة» اختيارهم اللذة الفانية على اللذة الباقية

rows.speaker: ابن فورك
rows.claim: Ibn Furak says ignorance means not knowing the full nature of the punishment; Ibn Atiyya weakens and rejects this explanation.
rows.anchor: ذكره ابن فورك. قال ابن عطية وضعف قوله هذا ورد عليه.

rows.speaker: ابن عباس والسدي
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas and al-Suddi define repentance ‘soon’ as before illness and death.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس والسدي: معناه قبل المرض والموت.

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Al-Dahhak says any repentance made before death counts as soon.
rows.anchor: وروي عن الضحاك أنه قال: كل ما كان قبل الموت فهو قريب.

rows.speaker: أبو مجلز والضحاك وعكرمة وابن زيد
rows.claim: Abu Mijlaz, al-Dahhak, Ikrima, Ibn Zayd, and others place the limit at seeing the angels and the death struggle, before a person loses control.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو مجلز والضحاك أيضا وعكرمة وابن زيد وغيرهم: قبل المعاينة للملائكة والسوق، وأن يغلب المرء على نفسه.

rows.speaker: محمود الوراق
rows.claim: Mahmud al-Warraq’s poem urges repentance before death and before the tongue is restrained, calling it provision for the repentant.
rows.anchor: قدم لنفسك توبة مرجوة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Repentance remains valid at this point because hope still exists and one can feel regret and resolve to stop the act.
rows.anchor: قال علماؤنا رحمهم الله: وإنما صحت التوبة منه في هذا الوقت لأن الرجاء باق

rows.speaker: ابن عمر
rows.claim: The Prophet says God accepts a servant’s repentance until the soul reaches the throat; al-Tirmidhi grades the report hasan gharib.
rows.anchor: وقد روى الترمذي عن ابن عمر عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال:

rows.speaker: الهروي
rows.claim: Al-Harawi explains ‘gurgling’ as the soul reaching the throat, like something being gargled.
rows.anchor: ومعنى ما لم يغرغر. ما لم تبلغ روحه حلقومه فيكون بمنزلة الشيء الذي يتغرغر به. قاله الهروي.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation takes ‘soon’ to mean soon after the sin and without persistence; repenting while healthy is better and leaves more hope for good works.
rows.anchor: وقيل: المعنى يتوبون على قرب عهد من الذنب من غير إصرار.

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan says anyone who shames a brother for a sin he has repented from will be afflicted with that sin.
rows.anchor: وروى صالح المري عن الحسن قال من عير أخاه بذنب قد تاب إلى الله منه ابتلاه الله به.

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan transmits God’s assurance to Iblis that repentance will not be barred while a person’s soul remains short of its final gasp.
rows.anchor: وقال الحسن أيضا: إن إبليس لما هبط قال: بعزتك لا أفارق ابن آدم ما دام الروح في جسده.

rows.speaker: ابن عباس وابن زيد وجمهور المفسرين
rows.claim: Repentance is not accepted once death appears and hope is gone, as Pharaoh’s confession while drowning did not benefit him; obligation has ended.
rows.anchor: وبهذا قال ابن عباس وابن زيد وجمهور المفسرين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who die in disbelief have no repentance in the afterlife and face eternal punishment; sinful believers face punishment without eternity if the sins mean lesser sins.
rows.anchor: وأما الكفار يموتون على كفرهم فلا توبة لهم في الآخرة،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An alternative reads ‘sins’ as disbelief, making the verse deny acceptance both to disbelievers repenting at death and to those repenting after death on Judgment Day.
rows.anchor: وقد قيل: إن السيئات هنا الكفر، فيكون المعنى وليست التوبة للكفار الذين يتوبون عند الموت،

rows.speaker: أبو العالية
rows.claim: Abu al-Aliya assigns the first repentance verse to believers and the second verse to hypocrites.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو العالية: نزل أول الآية في المؤمنين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here, those committing sins are people who persist until the death struggle and seeing the Angel of Death; repentance then is too late.
rows.anchor: يعني الشرق والنزع ومعاينة ملك الموت.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase describing painful punishment means painful and lasting; the surrounding discussion has already been explained.
rows.anchor: أي وجيعا دائما. وقد تقدم.

rows.speaker: المشركون
rows.claim: The polytheists objected to sitting with poor believers such as Salman, Suhayb, Bilal, and Khabbab, and asked that they be dismissed; the Prophet considered it but did not expel them.
rows.anchor: ولا نرضى بمجالسة أمثال هؤلاء يعنون سلمان وصهيبا وبلالا وخبابا فاطردهم عنك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet inclined toward their request only in hope of converting them and their people, thinking it would neither harm nor diminish the poor companions; revelation forbade the contemplated expulsion.
rows.anchor: وكان النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم إنما مال إلى ذلك طمعا في إسلامهم، وإسلام قومهم،

rows.speaker: سعد بن أبي وقاص
rows.claim: In Muslim’s report, Sa‘d and five other companions were present when the polytheists asked the Prophet to dismiss them, and revelation came after he reflected on the request.
rows.anchor: روى مسلم عن سعد بن أبي وقاص قال: كنا مع النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ستة نفر،

rows.speaker: ابن عباس ومجاهد والحسن
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, and al-Hasan interpret morning and evening invocation as keeping the obligatory prayers in congregation.
rows.anchor: قاله ابن عباس ومجاهد والحسن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other explanations take the invocation as remembrance and Qur’an recitation, or as prayers at daybreak and evening for guidance and forgiveness.
rows.anchor: وقيل: الذكر وقراءة القرآن. ويحتمل أن يريد الدعاء في أول النهار وآخره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘Seeking His face’ can mean sincerely seeking God’s obedience, or seeking God Himself, who is described as possessing the Face.
rows.anchor: أي طاعته، والإخلاص فيها، أي يخلصون في عبادتهم وأعمالهم لله،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Morning and evening are specified because people are usually occupied then, so one devoted to worship during busy hours is still more devoted in free time.
rows.anchor: وخص الغداة والعشي بالذكر لأن الشغل غالب فيهما على الناس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet later obeyed the command in 18:28 to remain with these worshippers, not looking away to seek worldly display.
rows.anchor: وكان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم بعد ذلك يصبر نفسه معهم كما أمره الله في قوله:

rows.speaker: خباب
rows.claim: Khabbab’s Ibn Majah report says al-Aqra‘ and ‘Uyayna sought a private session because Arab delegations might see them with poor believers; the Prophet agreed before revelation forbade dismissing them.
rows.anchor: عن خباب في قول الله عز وجل: { ولا تطرد الذين يدعون ربهم بالغداة والعشي }

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: After revelation, the Prophet sat with the poor companions and did not rise until they chose to leave.
rows.anchor: وكان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يجلس معنا فإذا أراد أن يقوم قام وتركنا

rows.speaker: سعد
rows.claim: Sa‘d reports that Quraysh rejected following six poor companions, including Sa‘d, Ibn Mas‘ud, Suhayb, ‘Ammar, al-Miqdad, and Bilal; revelation answered their demand.
rows.anchor: عن سعد قال: نزلت هذه الآية فينا ستة، في وفي ابن مسعود وصهيب وعمار والمقداد وبلال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘You are not responsible for their account’ means their judgment and provision belong to God, as do the Prophet’s; the first min is partitive and the second emphatic extra.
rows.anchor: الأولى للتبعيض، والثانية زائدة للتوكيد.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Since God alone provides and judges, the Prophet must receive and sit with them; expelling them to accommodate people of lesser faith would be injustice.
rows.anchor: فأقبل عليهم وجالسهم ولا تطردهم مراعاة لحق من ليس على مثل حالهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The warning is instruction for others, not evidence that the Prophet actually expelled anyone; it resembles the conditional warning against shirk though he would never commit it.
rows.anchor: وحاشاه من وقوع ذلك منه، وإنما هذا بيان للأحكام،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The syntax makes ‘then you would expel them’ a result of the preceding negation and ‘so you would be unjust’ a result of the prohibition; the clauses can also be reordered.
rows.anchor: نصب بالفاء في جواب النهي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse and report forbid elevating people for status or fine clothing and despising those who are obscure or poorly dressed.
rows.anchor: وقد حصل من قوة الآية والحديث النهي عن أن يعظم أحد لجاهه ولثوبه،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘The weighing that day is true’ can be parsed as subject and predicate, with ‘true’ as an adjective, or with ‘true’ as an accusative verbal noun.
rows.anchor: قوله تعالى: { والوزن يومئذ الحق } ابتداء وخبر. ويجوز أن يكون { الحق } نعته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse means deeds are weighed on the balance; Ibn Umar says the records of people’s deeds are weighed, which Qurtubi calls correct based on transmitted reports.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عمر: توزن صحائف أعمال العباد. وهذا هو الصحيح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view says the balance is the book in which people’s deeds are written.
rows.anchor: وقيل: الميزان الكتاب الذي فيه أعمال الخلق.

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid says the good and evil deeds themselves are weighed.
rows.anchor: وقال مجاهد: الميزان الحسنات والسيئات بأعيانها.

rows.speaker: مجاهد والضحاك والأعمش
rows.claim: Mujahid, al-Dahhak, and al-A‘mash take weighing and balance as metaphors for justice and judgment, as ordinary speech uses weight to mean equivalence.
rows.anchor: وعنه أيضا والضحاك والأعمش: الوزن والميزان بمعنى العدل والقضاء

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj accepts the metaphor as linguistically sound, but Qurtubi prefers the sound reports affirming a real balance.
rows.anchor: قال الزجاج: هذا سائغ من جهة اللسان، والأولى أن يتبع ما جاء في الأسانيد الصحاح

rows.speaker: القشيري
rows.claim: Al-Qushayri argues that metaphorizing the balance would also invite metaphorizing the Path, Paradise and Fire, jinn, and angels; the early community accepted these descriptions literally.
rows.anchor: وقد أجمعت الأمة في الصدر الأول على الأخذ بهذه الظواهر من غير تأويل

rows.speaker: المعتزلة
rows.claim: The Mu‘tazilites deny the balance because accidents cannot be weighed and do not subsist independently.
rows.anchor: وقد أنكرت المعتزلة الميزان بناء منهم على أن الأعراض يستحيل وزنها

rows.speaker: بعض المتكلمين
rows.claim: Some theologians say God turns accidents into bodies for weighing; Qurtubi rejects this and holds that written records make the scales heavier or lighter.
rows.anchor: ومن المتكلمين من يقول: إن الله تعالى يقلب الأعراض أجساما فيزنها يوم القيامة.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qurtubi’s preferred account is that deeds written in records are placed in the balance’s pans, as the report of the shahada card demonstrates.
rows.anchor: والصحيح أن الموازين تثقل بالكتب التي فيها الأعمال مكتوبة

rows.speaker: صفوان بن محرز
rows.claim: A Sahih Muslim narration from Safwan preserves Ibn Umar’s report of the Prophet’s conversation with God about the believer’s record.
rows.anchor: وفي صحيح مسلم عن صفوان بن محرز

rows.speaker: ابن عمر
rows.claim: The Prophet says God draws a believer close, makes him acknowledge his sins, then forgives him and gives him his record of good deeds; disbelievers and hypocrites are publicly exposed.
rows.anchor: يدنى المؤمن من ربه يوم القيامة حتى يضع عليه كنفه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The believer’s delivery of a record of good deeds proves deeds are written in records and weighed.
rows.anchor: دليل على أن الأعمال تكتب في الصحف وتوزن.

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن عمرو
rows.claim: A hadith describes a man’s ninety-nine vast records outweighed by a small card affirming God’s oneness and Muhammad’s messengership; al-Tirmidhi adds that nothing outweighs God’s name and grades it hasan gharib.
rows.anchor: وروى ابن ماجه من حديث عبد الله بن عمرو قال قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The plural ‘balances’ may mean multiple scales, one for each class of deed, or a single balance expressed in the plural, like travel by ships or mules.
rows.anchor: وقيل: يجوز أن يكون هناك موازين للعامل الواحد يوزن بكل ميزان منها صنف من أعماله.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another grammatical interpretation takes ‘balances’ as the plural of weighed things, meaning the deeds being weighed rather than the scales themselves.
rows.anchor: وقيل: الموازين جمع موزون، لا جمع ميزان. أراد بالموازين الأعمال الموزونة.

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas describes a balance with a tongue and two pans: the believer’s work in its best form makes good deeds outweigh sins, while the disbeliever’s ugly work falls short and he enters the Fire.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: توزن الحسنات والسيئات في ميزان له لسان وكفتان

rows.speaker: ابن فورك
rows.claim: The idea that God turns each deed into a substance whose material form is weighed resembles Ibn Abbas’s account, but Ibn Furak and others reject it.
rows.anchor: وما أشار إليه ابن عباس قريب مما قيل: يخلق الله تعالى كل جزء من أعمال العباد جوهرا

rows.speaker: القشيري
rows.claim: Al-Qushayri reports that the Prophet places a small card in the balance when a believer’s good deeds are light; it bears the reward of the believer’s prayers for the Prophet, repaid when most needed.
rows.anchor: ذكره القشيري في تفسيره

rows.speaker: القشيري
rows.claim: Al-Qushayri explains that bitāqa, with kasra on its first letter, means a small slip recording goods in Egyptian usage.
rows.anchor: وذكر أن البطاقة بكسر الباء رقعة فيها رقم المتاع بلغة أهل مصر

rows.speaker: محمد بن يحيى
rows.claim: Ibn Majah’s Muhammad ibn Yahya likewise says bitāqa means a slip of paper, as Egyptians call a slip.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن ماجه: قال محمد بن يحيى: البطاقة الرقعة، وأهل مصر يقولون للرقعة بطاقة.

rows.speaker: حذيفة
rows.claim: Hudhayfa says Gabriel oversees the scales; an oppressor’s good deeds repay victims, or the victims’ sins are transferred to him if his good deeds run out.
rows.anchor: وقال حذيفة: صاحب الموازين يوم القيامة جبريل عليه السلام،

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A report says God tells Adam to watch his descendants’ deeds: whoever’s good outweighs evil by even a grain enters Paradise, and whoever’s evil prevails enters Hell, for God punishes only the unjust.
rows.anchor: وروي عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Each community has a fixed term known to God; the hour is used because it is the smallest named time, and a person’s appointed death cannot be delayed or advanced.
rows.anchor: قوله تعالى: { ولكل أمة أجل } أي وقت مؤقت. { فإذا جاء أجلهم } أي الوقت المعلوم عند الله عز وجل.

rows.speaker: ابن سيرين
rows.claim: Ibn Sirin reads the phrase with the plural ‘their appointed times.’
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن سيرين «جاء آجالهم» بالجمع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A person’s ajal is the time God knows the living person will certainly die, not a time that is impossible for God to delay in power.
rows.anchor: وهو وقت لا يجوز تأخير موته عنه، لا من حيث إنه ليس مقدورا تأخيره.

rows.speaker: كثير من المعتزلة
rows.claim: Most Mu‘tazilites, with a few exceptions, say a murdered person dies before the appointed term and would otherwise have lived; Qurtubi calls this wrong.
rows.anchor: وقال كثير من المعتزلة إلا من شذ منهم: إن المقتول مات بغير أجله الذي ضرب له،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The victim dies because God takes the soul at the moment of the blow, not because the killer’s act independently causes death; retaliation punishes the killer’s transgression and prevents social ruin.
rows.anchor: بل من أجل ما فعله الله من إزهاق نفسه عند الضرب له

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says Quraysh circled the Kaaba naked, clapping and whistling as worship in their own view.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: كانت قريش تطوف بالبيت عراة، يصفقون ويصفرون فكان ذلك عبادة في ظنهم.

rows.speaker: مجاهد والسدي وابن عمر
rows.claim: Mujahid, al-Suddi, and Ibn Umar define al-muka as whistling and al-tasdiya as clapping; Antara’s verse uses muka for a sound.
rows.anchor: والمكاء: الصفير. والتصدية: التصفيق قاله مجاهد والسدي وابن عمر رضي الله عنهم.

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi says al-muka is whistling like the white bird in the Hijaz called al-muka, supported by a poet’s line about the bird.
rows.anchor: على لحن طائر أبيض بالحجاز يقال له المكاء

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada offers the alternative that al-muka means handclapping and al-tasdiya means shouting.
rows.anchor: قتادة: المكاء ضرب بالأيدي، والتصدية صياح.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On either interpretation, dancing, clapping, and swooning by ignorant Sufis is reprehensible imitation of polytheists at the Kaaba.
rows.anchor: ففيه رد على الجهال من الصوفية الذين يرقصون ويصفقون ويصعقون

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid also interprets al-muka as putting fingers in the mouth and al-tasdiya as whistling to distract Muhammad from prayer.
rows.anchor: وروى ابن جريج وابن أبي نجيح عن مجاهد أنه قال: المكاء إدخالهم أصابعهم في أفواههم. والتصدية: الصفير

rows.speaker: النحاس
rows.claim: Al-Nahhas says the familiar Arabic usage is Ibn Umar’s: maka means to whistle and sada means to clap, supported by Abu Ubayda and a line by Amr ibn al-Itnaba.
rows.anchor: المعروف في اللغة ما روي عن ابن عمر

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير وابن زيد
rows.claim: Sa‘id ibn Jubayr and Ibn Zayd explain al-tasdiya as blocking people from the Sacred House, deriving it from a form with two original d letters.
rows.anchor: معنى التصدية صدهم عن البيت فالأصل على هذا تصددة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘Distinguishing the foul from the good’ means separating disbeliever from believer, or more generally sorting all kinds of deeds, spending, and other things.
rows.anchor: أي المؤمن من الكافر. وقيل: هو عام في كل شيء، من الأعمال والنفقات وغير ذلك.

rows.speaker: مجاهد وأبو مالك
rows.claim: Mujahid and Abu Malik say the three were left behind from repentance.
rows.anchor: قيل: عن التوبة عن مجاهد وأبي مالك.

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada says they were left behind from the Tabuk campaign.
rows.anchor: وقال قتادة: عن غزوة تبوك.

rows.speaker: محمد بن زيد
rows.claim: Muhammad ibn Zayd explains the phrase as their being left behind, since leaving someone means separating while he remains seated.
rows.anchor: وحكي عن محمد بن زيد معنى «خلفوا» تركوا

rows.speaker: عكرمة بن خالد
rows.claim: Ikrima ibn Khalid reads the word to mean they remained in the Prophet’s wake.
rows.anchor: وقرأ عكرمة بن خالد «خلفوا» أي أقاموا بعقب رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم.

rows.speaker: جعفر بن محمد
rows.claim: Ja‘far ibn Muhammad is reported to have read the word as ‘they dissented.’
rows.anchor: وروي عن جعفر بن محمد أنه قرأ «خالفوا»

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The preferred explanation is that the three were deferred and their case postponed: unlike hypocrites or excused absentees, the Prophet delayed judgment until revelation, as the sound reports establish.
rows.anchor: وقيل: «خلفوا» أي أرجئوا وأخروا عن المنافقين فلم يقض فيهم بشيء.

rows.speaker: كعب بن مالك
rows.claim: Ka‘b clarifies that ‘left behind’ refers to the Prophet postponing their case after accepting the others’ excuses, not their failure to join the campaign.
rows.anchor: وليس الذي ذكر الله مما خلفنا تخلفنا عن الغزو، وإنما هو تخليفه إيانا وإرجاؤه أمرنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The three were Ka‘b ibn Malik, Murara ibn al-Rabi‘ al-‘Amiri, and Hilal ibn Umayya al-Waqifi, all from the Ansar.
rows.anchor: هم: كعب بن مالك، ومرارة بن ربيعة العامري، وهلال بن أمية الواقفي، وكلهم من الأنصار.

rows.speaker: كعب بن مالك
rows.claim: Ka‘b says he had never missed a campaign except Tabuk and Badr; no one was reproached for Badr because the Muslims had set out for the Quraysh caravan and unexpectedly met their enemy.
rows.anchor: عن كعب بن مالك قال: لم أتخلف عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم في غزوة غزاها قط إلا في غزوة تبوك

rows.speaker: كعب بن مالك
rows.claim: Ka‘b says the pledge at al-‘Aqaba mattered more to him than participation at Badr, despite Badr’s greater public fame.
rows.anchor: وما أحب أن لي بها مشهد بدر، وإن كانت بدر أذكر في الناس منها،

rows.speaker: كعب بن مالك
rows.claim: Ka‘b had never been stronger or wealthier than before Tabuk and gathered two mounts, while the expedition meant extreme heat, long travel, desert, and a large enemy.
rows.anchor: والله ما جمعت قبلها راحلتين قط حتى جمعتهما في تلك الغزوة

rows.speaker: كعب بن مالك
rows.claim: The Prophet announced the destination openly so Muslims could prepare; their large numbers were not recorded in a register, making a would-be absentee think revelation might not expose him.
rows.anchor: فأخبرهم بوجهه الذي يريد، والمسلمون مع رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم كثير، ولا يجمعهم كتاب حافظ

rows.speaker: كعب بن مالك
rows.claim: Ripe fruit and shade drew Ka‘b’s attention; he kept postponing preparations, assuming he could catch up, until the army had gone too far.
rows.anchor: وغزا رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم تلك الغزوة حين طابت الثمار والظلال فأنا إليها أصعر،

rows.speaker: كعب بن مالك
rows.claim: After the departure, Ka‘b felt isolated because he saw only a suspected hypocrite or someone excused by God among those left in Medina.
rows.anchor: يحزنني أني لا أرى لي أسوة إلا رجلا مغموصا عليه في النفاق

rows.speaker: كعب بن مالك
rows.claim: At Tabuk the Prophet asked about Ka‘b; one man blamed his clothes and vanity, but Mu‘adh ibn Jabal defended him as a man known for good, and the Prophet kept silent.
rows.anchor: فقال وهو جالس في القوم بتبوك: «ما فعل كعب بن مالك»؟

rows.speaker: كعب بن مالك
rows.claim: The Prophet recognized the approaching figure as Abu Khaythama, who had donated a measure of dates and been mocked by hypocrites.
rows.anchor: فقال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: «كن أبا خيثمة» فإذا هو أبو خيثمة الأنصاري،

rows.speaker: كعب بن مالك
rows.claim: As the Prophet returned, Ka‘b considered a lie but chose truth; on arrival the Prophet prayed two units in the mosque and received over eighty absentees, accepting their oaths outwardly and leaving their inner truth to God.
rows.anchor: فأجمعت صدقه، وصبح رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قادما، وكان إذا قدم من سفر بدأ بالمسجد

rows.speaker: كعب بن مالك
rows.claim: Ka‘b confessed to the Prophet that he had no excuse and had been able and wealthy enough to go; he said a false excuse might satisfy the Prophet but anger God.
rows.anchor: والله ما كان لي عذر، والله ما كنت قط أقوى ولا أيسر مني حين تخلفت عنك.

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet said Ka‘b had spoken truthfully and ordered him to wait until God decided his case.
rows.anchor: أما هذا فقد صدق فقم حتى يقضي الله فيك

rows.speaker: كعب بن مالك
rows.claim: Men from Banu Salama urged Ka‘b to invent an excuse, and he nearly returned to retract his truth; hearing Murara and Hilal had done likewise steadied him.
rows.anchor: فوالله ما زالوا يؤنبوني حتى أردت أن أرجع إلى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فأكذب نفسي

rows.speaker: كعب بن مالك
rows.claim: The Prophet singled out the three for a ban on speaking; after fifty nights of estrangement, Ka‘b continued prayer and market visits while the others stayed home weeping.
rows.anchor: فلبثنا على ذلك خمسين ليلة فأما صاحباي فاستكانا وقعدا في بيوتهما يبكيان

rows.speaker: كعب بن مالك
rows.claim: Ka‘b sought reassurance from his cousin Abu Qatada, but after repeated questions about his love for God and the Messenger, Abu Qatada answered only that God and His Messenger know.
rows.anchor: فقلت له: يا أبا قتادة أنشدك بالله! هل تعلمن أني أحب الله ورسوله؟

rows.speaker: كعب بن مالك
rows.claim: A Syrian merchant delivered a letter from the king of Ghassan offering Ka‘b refuge; Ka‘b regarded it as another trial and burned it.
rows.anchor: فدفع إلي كتابا من ملك غسان، وكنت كاتبا فقرأته

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: After forty of the fifty nights, the Prophet ordered the three to separate from their wives without divorcing them; Hilal’s wife could serve him but not have marital relations.
rows.anchor: إن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يأمرك أن تعتزل امرأتك

rows.speaker: كعب بن مالك
rows.claim: Ka‘b declined to request the same service permission given to Hilal’s wife, unsure what the Prophet would say to a young man.
rows.anchor: فقلت: لا أستأذن فيها رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم، وما يدريني ماذا يقول رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: كعب بن مالك
rows.claim: On the fiftieth morning, while he sat under the constriction described in the verse, a herald on Mount Sala announced good news and Ka‘b prostrated, recognizing relief.
rows.anchor: سمعت صوت صارخ أوفى على سلع يقول بأعلى صوته: يا كعب بن مالك أبشر.

rows.speaker: كعب بن مالك
rows.claim: The Prophet announced God’s acceptance after the dawn prayer; people congratulated Ka‘b, and Talha ibn Ubayd Allah ran to greet him, the only Muhajir to do so.
rows.anchor: فآذن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم الناس بتوبة الله علينا حين صلى صلاة الفجر

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet told Ka‘b that this was the best day since his birth and confirmed that the good news came from God.
rows.anchor: أبشر بخير يوم مر عليك منذ ولدتك أمك

rows.speaker: كعب بن مالك
rows.claim: Ka‘b offered all his property as charity for repentance, but the Prophet advised him to keep some; Ka‘b kept his share at Khaybar and pledged to speak only truth.
rows.anchor: أمسك عليك بعض مالك فهو خير لك

rows.speaker: كعب بن مالك
rows.claim: Ka‘b greeted the Prophet after prayer but received no answer and saw him turn away whenever Ka‘b looked toward him.
rows.anchor: هل حرك شفتيه برد السلام أم لا!

rows.speaker: كعب بن مالك
rows.claim: Ka‘b says the revealed passage included God’s repentance for the Prophet and believers, the three left behind, and the command to fear God and stay with the truthful.
rows.anchor: فأنزل الله عز وجل: { لقد تاب الله على النبي والمهاجرين والأنصار الذين اتبعوه في ساعة العسرة }

rows.speaker: كعب بن مالك
rows.claim: After Islam, Ka‘b considered truthful speech his greatest blessing; lying would have destroyed him like the liars, whom God censured severely.
rows.anchor: ما أنعم الله علي من نعمة قط بعد إذ هداني الله للإسلام أعظم في نفسي من صدقي رسول الله

rows.speaker: كعب بن مالك
rows.claim: Ka‘b again explains that the three were deferred from the accepted excuse-makers, so ‘left behind’ means their case was postponed rather than that they failed to campaign.
rows.anchor: وإنما هو تخليفه إيانا وإرجاؤه أمرنا عمن حلف له واعتذر إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘The earth narrowed despite its breadth’ means that the three were socially shunned, neither dealt with nor spoken to; the passage supports shunning sinners until they repent.
rows.anchor: وفي هذا دليل على هجران أهل المعاصي حتى يتوبوا.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their own selves narrowed through grief and loneliness caused by the companions’ coldness.
rows.anchor: أي ضاقت صدورهم بالهم والوحشة، وبما لقوه من الصحابة من الجفوة.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They became certain that only God could grant them pardon and accept their repentance.
rows.anchor: أي تيقنوا أن لا ملجأ يلجئون إليه في الصفح عنهم وقبول التوبة منهم إلا إليه

rows.speaker: أبو بكر الوراق
rows.claim: Abu Bakr al-Warraq defines sincere repentance by the distress of the earth and self, as in Ka‘b and his two companions.
rows.anchor: قال أبو بكر الوراق: التوبة النصوح أن تضيق على التائب الأرض بما رحبت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God began the process by accepting their repentance, enabling them to repent; divine acceptance precedes the human act of repentance.
rows.anchor: فبدأ بالتوبة منه

rows.speaker: أبو زيد
rows.claim: Abu Zayd describes four reversals: he thought he first loved God, pleased Him, remembered Him, and repented, but God had first loved, approved, remembered, and accepted him.
rows.anchor: قال أبو زيد: غلطت في أربعة أشياء: في الابتداء مع الله تعالى، ظننت أني أحبه فإذا هو أحبني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An alternative reads ‘so that they might repent’ as ‘so that they remain steadfast in repentance,’ as in the command for believers to believe.
rows.anchor: وقيل: المعنى ثم تاب عليهم ليثبتوا على التوبة كما قال تعالى:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another interpretation says God gave them respite and did not hasten punishment, unlike the punishment imposed on the Jews.
rows.anchor: وقيل: أي فسح لهم ولم يعجل عقابهم كما فعل بغيرهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The parable portrays worldly life as fleeting, vanishing, and of little value or pleasure; its condition resembles water from the sky, with the comparison particle in a nominative construction.
rows.anchor: أي صفة الحياة الدنيا في فنائها وزوالها وقلة خطرها والملاذ بها كماء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase ‘which We sent down from heaven’ describes the water; Qurtubi promises fuller treatment of this comparison in al-Kahf.
rows.anchor: «أنزلناه من السماء» نعت ل «ماء»

rows.speaker: نافع
rows.claim: Nafi‘ pauses after ‘it mixed’: water mixes into the earth, then the vegetation of the earth grows by that water; vegetation is the subject of the next clause.
rows.anchor: روي عن نافع أنه وقف على «فاختلط» أي فاختلط الماء بالأرض،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Without Nafi‘’s pause, the vegetation is the subject of ‘mixed’: it mixes with the rain, drinks it, and becomes moist, beautiful, and green; ikhtilat means interpenetration.
rows.anchor: وعلى مذهب من لم يقف على «فاختلط» مرفوع باختلط أي اختلط النبات بالمطر،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People eat grain, fruit, and vegetables from the vegetation, while livestock eat pasture, straw, and barley.
rows.anchor: قوله تعالى: { مما يأكل الناس } من الحبوب والثمار والبقول. { والأنعام } من الكلإ والتبن والشعير.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The earth takes its full beauty and adornment, hence gold is called ornament; ‘and it was adorned’ derives from tazayyanat with assimilation and a joining hamza.
rows.anchor: والزخرف كمال حسن الشيء ومنه قيل للذهب: زخرف.

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود وأبي بن كعب
rows.claim: Ibn Mas‘ud and Ubayy read the unassimilated original form, ‘and it adorns itself.’
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن مسعود وأبي بن كعب «وتزينت» على الأصل.

rows.speaker: الحسن والأعرج وأبو العالية
rows.claim: Al-Hasan, al-A‘raj, and Abu al-A‘liya read ‘and it brought forth its adornment,’ using the verb in its original form.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الحسن والأعرج وأبو العالية «وأزينت» أي أتت بالزينة عليها،

rows.speaker: عوف بن أبي جميلة الأعرابي
rows.claim: ‘Awf ibn Abi Jamilah says his elders read the form waziyānat; al-Muqaddami transmits wazāyanat, from tazāyanat with assimilation.
rows.anchor: وقال عوف بن أبي جميلة الأعرابي: قرأ أشياخنا «وازيانت»

rows.speaker: الشعبي وقتادة
rows.claim: Al-Sha‘bi and Qatada read the verb as ‘azayyanat,’ on the af‘alat pattern.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الشعبي وقتادة «وأزينت» مثل أفعلت.

rows.speaker: أبو عثمان النهدي
rows.claim: Abu Uthman al-Nahdi transmits three additional forms: az-zayyanat, zayānat, and azya’ant with hamza.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبو عثمان النهدي «وازينت» مثل افعلت،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘Its people thought they had power over it’ means they were certain they could harvest and benefit from it; the pronoun may refer to the earth, its yield, or its adornment.
rows.anchor: قوله تعالى: { وظن أهلها } أي أيقن. { أنهم قادرون عليها } أي على حصادها والانتفاع بها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s command arriving means either His punishment or His order that the land be destroyed; night and day are temporal adverbs.
rows.anchor: أي عذابنا، أو أمرنا بهلاكها.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘Harvested’ means cut down with nothing remaining; it is masculine because fa‘il has the sense of maf‘ul, and Abu Ubayda defines it as uprooted completely.
rows.anchor: ولم يؤنث لأنه فعيل بمعنى مفعول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘As though it had not flourished yesterday’ comes from ghaniya, to reside and inhabit; al-maghani are inhabited homes, while Qatada glosses it as not having enjoyed prosperity.
rows.anchor: { كأن لم تغن بالأمس } أي لم تكن عامرة من غني إذا أقام فيه وعمره.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Labid’s line supplies a linguistic example for ghaniya, ‘to inhabit’ or dwell in a place.
rows.anchor: وغنيت سبتا قبل مجرى داحس

rows.speaker: قراءة العامة
rows.claim: The common reading uses the feminine verb taghn because its grammatical subject is the earth.
rows.anchor: وقراءة العامة «تغن» بالتاء لتأنيث الأرض.

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada reads yaghnu with yā’, referring to the adornment; the crop’s sudden destruction illustrates the same fate of worldly life.
rows.anchor: وقرأ قتادة «يغن» بالياء، يذهب به إلى الزخرف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: To detail the signs means to make them clear for people who reflect on God’s signs.
rows.anchor: أي نبينها. { لقوم يتفكرون } في آيات الله.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase ‘as though they had not stayed’ abbreviates ‘as though they had not stayed in their graves’; the resurrection’s terror makes the grave seem as short as an hour.
rows.anchor: قوله تعالى: { ويوم يحشرهم كأن لم يلبثوا } بمعنى كأنهم فخففت، أي كأنهم لم يلبثوا في قبورهم

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says people view their whole earthly lifetimes as an hour when compared with eternity.
rows.anchor: رأوا أن طول أعمارهم في مقابلة الخلود كساعة

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: Al-Kalbi says people recognize one another as they did in life after leaving the graves; their recognition is reproach and exposure, not compassion.
rows.anchor: يعرف بعضهم بعضا كمعرفتهم في الدنيا إذا خرجوا من قبورهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One view says recognition ends at the sight of Judgment’s terrors, while Qurtubi prefers the view that reproach continues, supported by scenes of mutual cursing and blaming leaders.
rows.anchor: وقيل: يبقى تعارف التوبيخ وهو الصحيح لقوله تعالى: { ولو ترى إذ الظالمون موقوفون }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘No close friend asks another’ and ‘no kinship among them’ mean no question prompted by mercy or sympathy, not that recognition and blame cease altogether.
rows.anchor: فمعناه لا يسأله سؤال رحمة وشفقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other views say resurrection has different locations, or that recognition means asking each other how long they stayed; Qurtubi calls the latter a good interpretation.
rows.anchor: وقيل: القيامة مواطن. وقيل: معنى «يتعارفون» يتساءلون، أي يتساءلون كم لبثتم

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Al-Dahhak says believers recognize one another with affection, while unbelievers receive no mutual affection.
rows.anchor: ذلك تعارف تعاطف المؤمنين والكافرون لا تعاطف عليهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who denied meeting God lost the reward of Paradise, either as a declaration after proof of resurrection or at the actual encounter where reprieve and repentance no longer help.
rows.anchor: قوله تعالى: { قد خسر الذين كذبوا بلقاء الله } أي بالعرض على الله.

rows.speaker: النحاس
rows.claim: Al-Nahhas says ‘they recognize one another’ could be the disbelievers saying that they have lost.
rows.anchor: قال النحاس: ويجوز أن يكون المعنى يتعارفون بينهم، يقولون هذا.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘They were not guided’ means they were not among those God knew to be guided.
rows.anchor: { وما كانوا مهتدين } يريد في علم الله.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When people demanded punishment, the Prophet was told he controls neither harm nor benefit for himself except as God wills, so he cannot control their punishment either.
rows.anchor: قوله تعالى: { قل لا أملك لنفسي ضرا ولا نفعا } لما استعجلوا النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم بالعذاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Every nation has a time fixed in God’s knowledge for destruction and punishment; when it arrives, no one can delay or advance it even by an hour.
rows.anchor: { لكل أمة أجل } أي لهلاكهم وعذابهم وقت معلوم في علمه سبحانه.

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One view attributes the words to God speaking to Pharaoh.
rows.anchor: قيل: هو من قول الله تعالى.

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Alternative attributions make Gabriel, Michael, or another angel the speaker addressing Pharaoh.
rows.anchor: وقيل: هو من قول جبريل. وقيل: ميكائيل، صلوات الله عليهما، أو غيرهما من الملائكة

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view says Pharaoh himself thought the words inwardly rather than speaking them aloud; Qurtubi compares God’s praise of an inward intention elsewhere.
rows.anchor: ولم يكن ثم قول باللسان بل وقع ذلك في قلبه فقال في نفسه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The comparison shows that genuine speech can be speech of the heart, since God describes the feeding intention of the righteous without requiring spoken wording.
rows.anchor: والكلام الحقيقي كلام القلب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When God sends punishment on a people, His practice is to remove the messengers and believers from among them and save them.
rows.anchor: إذا أنزلنا بقوم عذابا أخرجنا من بينهم الرسل والمؤمنين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘A duty upon Us’ means God’s promise must be fulfilled because He has stated it and never breaks His word.
rows.anchor: أي واجبا علينا لأنه أخبر ولا خلف في خبره

rows.speaker: يعقوب
rows.claim: Ya‘qub reads the verb for saving the messengers in a light form.
rows.anchor: وقرأ يعقوب. «ثم ننجي» مخففا.

rows.speaker: الكسائي وحفص ويعقوب
rows.claim: Al-Kisa’i, Hafs, and Ya‘qub read the verb ‘save the believers’ in a light form, while the other readers use the doubled form; both are eloquent forms with the same meaning.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الكسائي وحفص ويعقوب. «ننجي المؤمنين» مخففا

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farra’ treats kāna as extra, explaining the jussive response in the verse.
rows.anchor: قوله تعالى: { من كان } كان زائدة، ولهذا جزم بالجواب فقال: { نوف إليهم }

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj reads man kāna as a jussive condition with nuwaf as its answer, meaning whoever wants; the shift from past to future is supported by Zuhayr’s poetry.
rows.anchor: وقال الزجاج: { من كان } في موضع جزم بالشرط، وجوابه { نوف إليهم } أي من يكن يريد

rows.speaker: الضحاك والنحاس
rows.claim: Al-Dahhak says the verse concerns disbelievers, and al-Nahhas prefers this because the next verse denies them any afterlife share beyond the Fire; worldly charity earns health and wealth only.
rows.anchor: واختلف العلماء في تأويل هذه الآية فقيل: نزلت في الكفار قاله الضحاك، واختاره النحاس بدليل الآية التي بعدها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view applies it to believers who intend only worldly reward: they receive full worldly recompense but punishment in the afterlife because their purpose was confined to this world.
rows.anchor: وقيل: المراد بالآية المؤمنون أي من أراد بعمله ثواب الدنيا عجل له الثواب ولم ينقص شيئا في الدنيا

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: A report about show-offs says they fasted, prayed, gave charity, fought, and recited to gain praise, and will be among the first fuel of Hell; Abu Hurayra wept, affirmed it, and recited these verses.
rows.anchor: رواه أبو هريرة، ثم بكى بكاء شديدا وقال: صدق رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: مجاهد وميمون بن مهران
rows.claim: Mujahid and Maymun ibn Mihran apply the verse generally to anyone who intends something other than God, whether or not the person has basic faith.
rows.anchor: وقيل: الآية عامة في كل من ينوي بعمله غير الله تعالى، كان معه أصل إيمان أو لم يكن قاله مجاهد وميمون ابن مهران

rows.speaker: ميمون بن مهران
rows.claim: Maymun says every good deed is repaid: a sincere Muslim receives reward in this world and the next, while a disbeliever receives it in this world alone.
rows.anchor: وقال ميمون بن مهران: ليس أحد يعمل حسنة إلا وفي ثوابها فإن كان مسلما مخلصا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A narrower view concerns people who joined the Prophet’s campaign for worldly spoils; Qurtubi rejects that limitation and prefers the general reading.
rows.anchor: وهذا خصوص والصحيح العموم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse’s rule that reward follows intention means a Ramadan fast not intended as the Ramadan fast does not count, nor does washing for cooling count as prayer ablution; the principle extends to similar acts.
rows.anchor: وتدلك هذه الآية على أن من صام في رمضان لا عن رمضان لا يقع عن رمضان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most scholars take this verse and similar statements in al-Shura and Ali Imran as unrestricted, then qualified by the verse on the immediate life: God grants what He wills to whomever He wills.
rows.anchor: الثالثة: ذهب أكثر العلماء إلى أن هذه الآية مطلقة

rows.speaker: الضحاك عن ابن عباس
rows.claim: Al-Dahhak transmits from Ibn Abbas that this verse was abrogated by the verse about whoever desires the immediate life.
rows.anchor: وروى الضحاك عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما في قوله: { من كان يريد الحياة الدنيا } أنها منسوخة بقوله: { من كان يريد العاجلة }.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qurtubi rejects abrogation here and prefers an unrestricted-versus-qualified reading; an apparently universal promise of answering prayer is similarly qualified by God’s will.
rows.anchor: والصحيح ما ذكرناه وأنه من باب الإطلاق والتقييد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abrogating statements of fact is impossible because truths cannot change and God cannot lie; reports about legal rulings may be abrogated, subject to scholarly debate.
rows.anchor: والنسخ في الأخبار لا يجوز لاستحالة تبدل الواجبات العقلية
